test_title: PYST 9: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Who founded Harijan Sangh and contended that the Shastras did not approve untouchability; and if they did, they should be disregarded?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Mahatma Gandhi** founded the **Harijan Sevak Sangh** on **30 September 1932**. This organization was established to eradicate **untouchability** in India and uplift the depressed classes. ***Hence, the statement about the founder is correct.***

• Gandhi strongly contended that the **Shastras** (ancient Hindu scriptures) did not provide any religious sanction for the practice of **untouchability**. He viewed it as a **social evil** that had crept into **Hinduism** over time.

• He famously argued that if any **scripture** were found to support **untouchability**, it should be **disregarded** as it would be contrary to the fundamental principles of **Truth** and **Non-violence** (Ahimsa).

• **Rabindranath Tagore** was a world-renowned poet and philosopher who founded **Visva-Bharati University** in **1921**. While he supported social reforms, he was not the founder of the **Harijan Sevak Sangh**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was a moderate political leader and the founder of the **Servants of India Society** in **1905**. He served as a mentor to Gandhi but passed away in **1915**, long before the **Harijan Sangh** was formed. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• **Jyotiba Phule** was a pioneering social reformer from **Maharashtra** who founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** in **1873**. Although he was a champion for the rights of the lower castes, he was not associated with the **Harijan Sevak Sangh** founded in the **20th century**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**

__

• **Harijan Sevak Sangh**: Originally named the **All India Anti-Untouchability League**, it was later renamed by Gandhi. The headquarters of the organization is located at **Kingsway Camp** in **Delhi**.

• **Leadership**: The first president of the **Harijan Sevak Sangh** was the prominent industrialist **Ghanshyam Das Birla**, and the first secretary was **Amritlal Thakkar**, popularly known as **Thakkar Bapa**.

• **Satyashodhak Samaj**: Founded by **Jyotiba Phule** in **Pune**, this society aimed to liberate the **Shudra** and **Untouchable** castes from exploitation by upper castes. Phule also wrote the famous book **Gulamgiri** in **1873**.

• **Servants of India Society**: Established by **Gokhale** in **Pune**, its objective was to train **national missionaries** for the service of India and to promote the true interests of the Indian people through constitutional means.

• **Visva-Bharati**: Located in **Santiniketan**, **West Bengal**, it was declared a **Central University** and an institution of national importance in **1951**. **Tagore** envisioned it as a place where the world makes a home in a single nest.

**Important Points__**

• **Poona Pact (1932)**: The **Harijan Sevak Sangh** was a direct outcome of the **Poona Pact** signed between **Mahatma Gandhi** and **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**. This pact was reached after Gandhi's fast in **Yerwada Jail** against the **Communal Award** of **Ramsay MacDonald**.

• **Harijan Journal**: To spread his message against **untouchability**, Gandhi started a weekly journal named **Harijan** in **1933**. He also published **Harijan Bandu** in **Gujarati** and **Harijan Sevak** in **Hindi**.

• **Harijan Tour**: Between **November 1933** and **July 1934**, Gandhi undertook a **nationwide tour** known as the **Harijan Tour**, covering about **20,000 kilometers** to collect funds (**Harijan Fund**) and mobilize public opinion against the practice of **untouchability**.
